sentence: This project looks for drug targets and compounds that could treat pediatric tumors lacking clinically actionable mutations, and tests them in mouse models.
This project tracks antimicrobial resistance in bacterial pathogens of veterinary concern, using whole genome sequence data.
This project studies how cells control the proteins that shape the cytoskeleton and give cells their polarity.
This project studies risk markers, early detection and ways to intervene in pre-malignant and early-stage cancer.
This project tests whether self-management interventions can reduce chronic musculoskeletal pain in adults in later life, in a randomized controlled trial.
This project tests whether transferring or stimulating gamma delta T cells can treat melanoma in humanized mouse models.
This project studies how gasdermin-mediated pyroptosis, a form of programmed cell death, is regulated, using live cell imaging.
This project builds a knowledgebase that collects information on perioperative organ injury from public data resources.
This project studies how gene mutations change hematopoietic stem cells and let mutant cells outgrow normal hematopoietic cells, causing a blood disease.
This project studies how one carbon metabolism and formate help T cells fight tumors.
This project studies how neutrophils and sensory neurons communicate in lung cancer.
This project builds human airway organoids and cell cultures to test how phage therapy works against Klebsiella pneumoniae infection.
This project tests androgen receptor inhibitors in a clinical trial for triple-negative breast cancer and looks for biomarkers that predict response.
This project studies how cell types in the human retina process visual information and send it to the brain.
This project uses deep learning on snoring and sleep-study data to find where the airway collapses in obstructive sleep apnea.
This project looks for mutations in the envelope protein that could help design a live-attenuated vaccine for West Nile virus.
This project studies how nerves, epithelial cells and immune cells on the ocular surface communicate in health and disease.
This project studies how a neuronal auto-antigen is linked to pain, in a rare condition called Paraneoplastic Syndrome.
This project repairs an inverted microscope used for imaging experiments with worms.
This project studies how methylglyoxal causes diabetic neuropathic pain through the integrated stress response in nociceptors.
